title.zh: 卷403 列傳一百九十 胜保 托明阿 陈金绶 德兴阿
title.en: Volume 403 Biographies 190: Sheng Bao, Tuo Ming A, Chen Jinshou, De Xing A
title.raw: 卷403 列傳一百九十 胜保 托明阿 陈金绶 德兴阿

sentences.zh: 勝保，字克齋，蘇完瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao, styled Kezhai, of the Suwan Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao, whose style was Kezhai, belonged to the Suwan Guwalgiya clan and was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年舉人，考授順天府教授。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang he became a provincial graduate; through examination he was appointed professor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twentieth year of the Daoguang reign and, after further examination, was appointed professor of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷贊善，大考二等，擢侍講，累遷祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting; in the grand examination he ranked second class, was promoted to Lecturer-in-Waiting, and by successive transfers became Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Reader-in-Waiting, he placed in the second class in the grand examination, was promoted to Lecturer-in-Waiting, and rose by stages to Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 屢上疏言事，甚著風采。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on public affairs and was highly noted for his moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial on affairs of state and won a strong reputation for forthright conduct.

sentences.zh: 歷光祿寺卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and as a Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，因天變上疏論時政，言甚切直，略謂：「廣西賊勢猖獗，廣東、湖南皆可憂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, citing celestial portents he submitted a memorial on current affairs, speaking with great bluntness; in summary he said: 'The bandits in Guangxi are raging fiercely, and both Guangdong and Hunan are cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, citing omens in the heavens, he memorialized on current affairs in language that was sharply direct. In substance he wrote: 'The rebels in Guangxi are raging out of control, and Guangdong and Hunan are both deeply worrying.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿督師無功，請明賞罰以振紀綱。

translations.literal: Sai Shang'a commands the army without achievement; please make rewards and punishments clear to revive discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a has led the armies without success; rewards and punishments should be made explicit so that discipline may be restored.

sentences.zh: 河決不治河員之罪，刑輕盜風日熾，應明敕法以肅典常。

translations.literal: When the river bursts its banks the river officials' crimes go unpunished; punishments are light and banditry grows daily fiercer; the law should be clearly proclaimed to enforce canonical norms.
translations.idiomatic: When floods breach the dikes, the officials responsible escape punishment; because penalties are too lenient, lawlessness grows worse by the day, and the statutes ought to be enforced clearly to uphold proper order.

sentences.zh: 臣工奏摺多留中，恐滋流弊。

translations.literal: Many memorials from officials are kept within the palace, which may breed lasting abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Too many officials' memorials are held back in the palace, a practice that is likely to breed lasting abuses.

sentences.zh: 一切事務，硃批多而諭旨少。

translations.literal: In all affairs there are many vermilion rescripts but few edicts of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: On every matter there are numerous vermilion rescripts but few formal edicts promulgated to the realm.

sentences.zh: 市井細民，時​​或私論聖德。

translations.literal: Petty townsfolk sometimes privately discuss the sage virtue of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Even common people in the markets sometimes whisper privately about the emperor's virtue.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下樞臣傳問疏末兩端，令直言無隱。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial entered, the Grand Council was ordered to inquire about the two points at the end of the memorial and to speak frankly without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the memorial reached the throne, the Grand Council was instructed to question him about the two closing points and to speak with complete candor.

sentences.zh: 覆奏曰：「硃批因事垂訓，臣工奉到遵行，他人不與聞，非若諭旨頒示天下。

translations.literal: In his reply he said: 'Vermilion rescripts instruct on particular matters; officials receive them and obey, but others do not hear of them, unlike edicts of instruction promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In his follow-up memorial he wrote: 'Vermilion rescripts teach lessons on particular cases; the official who receives one obeys it, but no one else learns of it, unlike an edict that is proclaimed to the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 近日諸臣條奏雖依議，而原奏之人不知；

translations.literal: Recently, although ministers' submissions are decided according to deliberation, the original submitter does not know the outcome;
translations.idiomatic: Lately, even when a minister's proposal is approved in deliberation, the minister who first submitted it is never told what was decided;

sentences.zh: 交部重案，覆奏依議，外人並不知作何發落。

translations.literal: in major cases referred to the ministries, when the reply memorial follows deliberation, outsiders altogether do not know what disposition was made.
translations.idiomatic: and in grave cases handed to the ministries, once the deliberated reply is filed, the public has no idea what sentence or outcome was imposed.

sentences.zh: 古者象魏懸書，俾眾屬目。

translations.literal: In antiquity proclamations were hung at the Elephant Watchtower so that the multitude could fix their eyes upon them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity edicts were posted at the Elephant Watchtower so that all could see them plainly.

sentences.zh: 似宜通行宣示，以昭朝廷之令甲，而杜胥吏之蔽欺。

translations.literal: It seems fitting to proclaim them throughout so as to display the court's ordinances and to stop clerks and petty officials from concealing and deceiving.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to announce decisions openly throughout the realm, both to make the court's commands visible and to shut off the concealment and fraud of clerks and runners.

sentences.zh: 至愚賤私議，或謂皇上勵精之心不如初政，或謂勤儉之德不及先皇。

translations.literal: As for the foolish and base private talk, some say the emperor's resolve to strive is not equal to the early years of his rule, or that his diligence and frugality do not match the previous emperor.
translations.idiomatic: As for vulgar private gossip, some say Your Majesty's zeal is no longer what it was at the start of the reign, while others say your thrift and austerity fall short of the late emperor's example.

sentences.zh: 今遊觀之所，煥然一新。

translations.literal: Now the places for touring and viewing are wholly renewed.
translations.idiomatic: The pleasure grounds and scenic sites have lately been refurbished until they look wholly new.

sentences.zh: 釋服之後，必將有適性陶情之事，現在內府已有採辦犁園服飾以備進御者。

translations.literal: After the mourning garments are laid aside there will surely be matters for fitting one's nature and cultivating feeling; already the Inner Palace has procured opera costumes and apparel to present to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ends, there will surely be occasions for ease and diversion, and the Inner Palace is already purchasing opera costumes and finery to present to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 夫鼓樂田獵，何損聖德。

translations.literal: Music, drums, and hunting in the fields—what harm do they do to sage virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Music, pageantry, and the hunt in themselves do no injury to sage virtue.

sentences.zh: 然自古帝王必先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂。

translations.literal: Yet from antiquity emperors and kings have first shared the empire's worries and only afterward shared its joys.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from antiquity true rulers have taken the empire's anxieties upon themselves before they have tasted its pleasures.

sentences.zh: 書曰：'無於水監，當於民監。

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'Do not take your mirror from water; take your mirror from the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: 'Do not mirror yourself in water; mirror yourself in the people.

sentences.zh: '誠不可不察也。

translations.literal: ' This truly cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is a lesson that truly cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 」文宗不懌，明諭指駁，以其意存諷諫，不之罪也。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Wenzong was displeased and issued an explicit edict rebutting him, but because his intent lay in admonition he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: ' Emperor Wenzong was displeased and issued an edict point by point to refute him, yet because his purpose was admonitory counsel, he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 尋因自行撤回封奏，降四品京堂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because he had on his own withdrawn a sealed memorial, he was demoted to a fourth-rank metropolitan official.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because he had withdrawn a sealed memorial on his own initiative, he was demoted to a fourth-rank post in the capital bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 會粵匪犯武昌，勝保疏陳辦賊方略，命馳往河南，交欽差大臣琦善差遣。

translations.literal: When Cantonese bandits attacked Wuchang, Sheng Bao memorialized strategies for dealing with the rebels and was ordered to hurry to Henan and placed under the orders of Imperial Commissioner Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cantonese rebels threatened Wuchang, Sheng Bao laid out a plan for suppressing them and was ordered posthaste to Henan, where he was placed at the disposal of Imperial Commissioner Qishan.

sentences.zh: 三年春，偕提督陳金綬率兵援湖北、安徽，而江寧告急。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, together with Regional Commander Chen Jinshou he led troops to relieve Hubei and Anhui, but Jiangning reported urgent danger.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he marched with Regional Commander Chen Jinshou to reinforce Hubei and Anhui, even as Jiangning sent desperate appeals for aid.

sentences.zh: 至則城已陷，駐兵江浦。

translations.literal: When he arrived the city had already fallen, and he encamped his troops at Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the city had already fallen, and he stationed his army at Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 勝保疏陳軍事稱旨，命以內閣學士會辦軍務，克浦口而賊陷揚州，偕陳金綬進剿。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao's memorials on military affairs pleased the throne; he was ordered as Grand Secretariat Academician to assist in military affairs, took Pukou, but the rebels captured Yangzhou, and together with Chen Jinshou he advanced to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao's reports on military affairs pleased the court, and he was appointed Grand Secretariat Academician to assist in the campaign. He recovered Pukou, but the rebels then seized Yangzhou, and he advanced with Chen Jinshou to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 擊賊鎮海寺南，破之，薄揚州城下，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He attacked the rebels south of Zhenhai Temple, defeated them, pressed close beneath Yangzhou's walls, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the rebels south of Zhenhai Temple, routed them, and pressed up to the walls of Yangzhou, for which he was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 又連破賊於天寧、廣儲門外。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly defeated the rebels outside Tianning and outside Guangchu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He won further victories over the rebels outside Tianning Temple and beyond Guangchu Gate.

sentences.zh: 奉命赴安徽勦賊，而賊已入河南，渡河圍懷慶。

translations.literal: Ordered to go to Anhui to suppress rebels, he found the rebels had already entered Henan, crossed the river, and besieged Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Anhui to suppress the rebels, he found they had already pushed into Henan, crossed the Yellow River, and were besieging Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 勝保會諸軍進擊，將軍托明阿軍其東，勝保軍其南。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao joined the various armies in the attack; General Tuo Ming'a's army was on the east and Sheng Bao's on the south.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao coordinated the allied armies in the assault: General Tuo Ming'a held the eastern sector and Sheng Bao the southern.

sentences.zh: 時督師大學士訥爾經額遙駐臨洺關，援軍數路久頓城下，惟二軍戰較力，命勝保幫辦河北軍務。

translations.literal: At the time the commanding Grand Secretary Ne'erjing'e remained far off at Linzhang Pass; relief forces on several routes had long stalled below the walls; only these two armies fought with real effort, and Sheng Bao was ordered to assist in Hebei military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander, Grand Secretary Ne'erjing'e, remained far to the rear at Linzhang Pass while relief columns on several routes had stalled for months beneath the walls. Only these two armies fought with real vigor, and Sheng Bao was ordered to assist in the Hebei campaign.

sentences.zh: 七月，分三路進攻賊壘，大破之，懷慶圍解，加都統銜，賜黃馬褂，予霍鑾巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they attacked the rebel stockades on three routes, inflicted a great defeat, and lifted the siege of Huaiqing; he was given the rank of Commandant-in-Chief, granted the yellow riding jacket, and awarded the title Huoluan Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they assaulted the rebel camps on three fronts and won a crushing victory that lifted the siege of Huaiqing. He was given the rank of Commandant-in-Chief, awarded the yellow riding jacket, and granted the title Huoluan Baturu.

sentences.zh: 賊竄山西，連陷數縣，諸軍遷延，惟勝保率善祿、西凌阿兵四千尾追，一破之封門山口，再破之平陽，繞出賊前，扼韓侯嶺，尋复洪洞、平陽。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into Shanxi and in succession took several counties; the armies delayed, but only Sheng Bao with Shanlu and Xiling'a and four thousand troops pursued in the rear, first defeating them at Fengmen Pass, again defeating them at Pingyang, circling ahead of the rebels, and holding Hanhou Ridge; soon he recovered Hongtong and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke into Shanxi and overran several counties in succession while other armies dawdled. Sheng Bao alone, with Shanlu and Xiling'a and four thousand men, pursued hard: he defeated them once at Fengmen Pass and again at Pingyang, swung ahead of their line, seized Hanhou Ridge, and soon recovered Hongtong and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 劾逗留諸將托雲保、董占元、烏勒欣泰等，罪之；

translations.literal: He impeached the delaying generals Tuo Yunbao, Dong Zhanyuan, Wulexintai, and others, and they were punished;
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the generals who had lingered—Tuo Yunbao, Dong Zhanyuan, Wulexintai, and others—and they were punished.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉勝保果勇有為，授欽差大臣，代訥爾經額督師，節制各路，特賜康熙朝安親王所進神雀刀，凡貽誤軍情者，副將以下立斬以聞。

translations.literal: An edict praised Sheng Bao as resolute, brave, and effective, appointed him Imperial Commissioner in place of Ne'erjing'e as commander, with authority over all routes; he was specially granted the divine sparrow blade presented by the Prince of An in the Kangxi reign; anyone who harmed military affairs, from deputy general downward, was to be summarily beheaded and reported.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended Sheng Bao as bold and effective, made him Imperial Commissioner in Ne'erjing'e's place as supreme commander with authority over every column, and specially granted him the 'divine sparrow' sword once presented by the Kangxi-era Prince of An. Anyone from deputy general downward who jeopardized operations was to be beheaded on the spot and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 賊既不得北竄，轉而南，由澤、潞間道入直隸境。

translations.literal: The rebels, unable to flee north, turned south and by the bypaths of Ze and Lu entered Zhili territory.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to break northward, the rebels turned south and slipped into Zhili by the mountain routes between Zezhou and Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 訥爾經額師潰於臨洺關，賊复猖獗，竄順德、趙州、正定。

translations.literal: Ne'erjing'e's army was routed at Linzhang Pass; the rebels again ran rampant and fled through Shunde, Zhaozhou, and Zhengding.
translations.idiomatic: Ne'erjing'e's army was routed at Linzhang Pass, the rebels surged out again, and they swept through Shunde, Zhaozhou, and Zhengding.

sentences.zh: 勝保由井陘一路迎截，坐追賊不力，鐫二級。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao moved by the Jingxing route to intercept head-on; for pursuing the rebels without force he was stripped of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao marched by the Jingxing road to block them, but because his pursuit had lacked vigor he was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 命惠親王綿愉為大將軍，科爾沁郡王僧格林沁為參贊大臣，駐軍涿州，直隸軍務仍責勝保專任，而以西凌阿、善祿副之。

translations.literal: Prince Mianyu of Hui was appointed Grand General, the Khorchin Prince Sengge Rinchen was made Assisting Commissioner, with troops encamped at Zhuozhou; Zhili military affairs were still charged solely to Sheng Bao, with Xiling'a and Shanlu as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mianyu of Hui was named Grand General and the Khorchin Prince Sengge Rinchen Assisting Commissioner, with headquarters at Zhuozhou. Zhili operations remained Sheng Bao's sole responsibility, with Xiling'a and Shanlu as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 賊東竄，由深州、河間窺天津，勝保轉戰追賊至靜海。

translations.literal: The rebels fled east, from Shenzhou and Hejian eyed Tianjin, and Sheng Bao fought in successive battles pursuing them to Jinghai.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bolted eastward, probing toward Tianjin from Shenzhou and Hejian, while Sheng Bao fought his way in pursuit as far as Jinghai.

sentences.zh: 賊由獨流分踞楊柳青，迭擊之，遂聚於靜海、獨流，負嵎久踞。

translations.literal: The rebels from Duliu divided forces and held Yangliuqing; he attacked them repeatedly, and they then gathered at Jinghai and Duliu, relying on their lair and holding long.
translations.idiomatic: From Duliu the rebels fanned out to seize Yangliuqing; he struck them again and again until they massed at Jinghai and Duliu, where they dug in and held their ground for a long time.

sentences.zh: 詔僧格林沁進軍合剿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sengge Rinchen to advance and join in the joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Sengge Rinchen forward to join the combined suppression.

sentences.zh: 四年春，賊突圍走阜城，追擊，殲賊數千，陣斃悍酋吉文元。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the rebels broke the encirclement and fled to Fucheng; in pursuit several thousand rebels were annihilated and the fierce chieftain Ji Wenyuan was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year the rebels broke out toward Fucheng. In the pursuit several thousand were destroyed and the fierce rebel leader Ji Wenyuan was killed on the field.

sentences.zh: 而援賊由江北偷渡黃河擾山東，命勝保移兵往剿，臨清失守，坐褫職，戴罪自效。

translations.literal: Meanwhile relief rebels from north of the river secretly crossed the Yellow River and harassed Shandong; Sheng Bao was ordered to move troops to suppress them; Linqing was lost, and for this he was stripped of office and told to redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile rebel reinforcements stole across the Yellow River from the north bank to ravage Shandong, and Sheng Bao was ordered to shift his forces thither. Linqing fell, he was stripped of his post for the lapse, and was ordered to redeem himself in the field.

sentences.zh: 尋破賊，克臨清，餘賊南走，追擊迭破之，解散甚眾。

translations.literal: Soon he defeated the rebels, recovered Linqing, the remnant rebels fled south, and in pursuit he repeatedly defeated them and disbanded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: He soon routed the rebels, retook Linqing, and as the survivors fled south he defeated them again and again and broke up large numbers of them.

sentences.zh: 及竄入豐縣，僅千餘人，蹙之河岸，悉數殲除。

translations.literal: When they fled into Feng County there were only a little more than a thousand; he pressed them to the riverbank and annihilated them to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: When the last band slipped into Feng County there were barely a thousand left; he cornered them on the riverbank and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，復職，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was restored to office and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived he was restored to office and promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁圍林鳳祥、李開芳於連鎮，久未下，命勝保回軍會剿。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen besieged Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang at Lianzhen but for a long time could not take it; Sheng Bao was ordered to return his army for the joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen had long besieged Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang at Lianzhen without success, and Sheng Bao was ordered to bring his troops back for a combined assault.

sentences.zh: 開芳突出，分股竄山東，勝保親率輕騎追之，賊陷高唐踞守，圍之數月不能克。

translations.literal: Kaifang broke out, divided forces and fled into Shandong; Sheng Bao personally led light cavalry in pursuit; the rebels took Gaotang and held it; he besieged it for months without being able to capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kaifang broke out, split his force, and fled into Shandong. Sheng Bao personally led light cavalry in pursuit, but the rebels seized Gaotang and held it, and though he besieged the city for months he could not take it.

sentences.zh: 迭詔詰責，褫職逮京治罪，遣戍新疆。

translations.literal: Edicts repeatedly rebuked him; he was stripped of office, arrested and sent to the capital for punishment, and banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Edict after edict rebuked him. He was stripped of office, brought to the capital for trial, and banished to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 直隸、山東賊既平，予藍翎侍衛，充伊犁領隊大臣。

translations.literal: After the rebels in Zhili and Shandong were pacified, he was made a Blue Feather Bodyguard and served as Brigade Commander at Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels in Zhili and Shandong had been pacified, he was made a Blue Feather Bodyguard and appointed Brigade Commander at Ili.

sentences.zh: 六年，召還，發往安徽軍營差遣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was recalled and sent to the Anhui army camp for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled from exile and dispatched to the Anhui theater.

sentences.zh: 七年，予副都統銜，幫辦河南軍務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the rank of Vice Commandant-in-Chief and assisted in Henan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was given the rank of Vice Commandant-in-Chief and assigned to assist in the Henan campaign.

sentences.zh: 捻匪方熾，勝保至，連破之方家集、烏龍集、柳溝集，克三河尖老巢。

translations.literal: Nian bandits were then at their height; when Sheng Bao arrived he in succession defeated them at Fangjiaji, Wulongji, and Liugouji, and took the old lair at Sanhejian.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian rebels were at the height of their power when Sheng Bao arrived. He defeated them in succession at Fangjiaji, Wulongji, and Liugouji and captured their stronghold at Sanhejian.

sentences.zh: 又克河關，复霍丘，大捷於正陽關，斬捻首魏藍奇等，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: He again took Heguan, recovered Huoqiu, won a great victory at Zhengyang Pass, beheaded the Nian chieftain Wei Lanqi and others, and was given the first-rank official's hat button.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Heguan, recovered Huoqiu, and won a major victory at Zhengyang Pass, where he beheaded the Nian leader Wei Lanqi and others. He was awarded the first-rank official's hat button.

sentences.zh: 八年，平酆家集、喬家廟、趙屯諸捻巢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he pacified the Nian lairs at Fengjiaji, Qiaojiamiao, Zhaotun, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he wiped out Nian strongholds at Fengjiaji, Qiaojiamiao, Zhaotun, and other sites.

sentences.zh: 粵匪大股圍固始，擊破之，殲賊萬餘，斬偽顯天侯卜占魁等，固始圍解。

translations.literal: A large Cantonese rebel force besieged Gushi; he attacked and defeated them, annihilated more than ten thousand rebels, beheaded the false Xiantian Marquis Bu Zhan'kui and others, and the siege of Gushi was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: A large Taiping column besieged Gushi; he broke the siege, killed more than ten thousand rebels, and beheaded the false 'Manifest Heaven Marquis' Bu Zhan'kui and others.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉謀勇兼優，遇都統缺出題奏，复黃馬褂、巴圖魯，免其弟廉保遣戍罪。

translations.literal: An edict praised his combined excellence in planning and courage; when a Commandant-in-Chief vacancy arose he was to be specially memorialized; he again received the yellow riding jacket and Baturu title, and his younger brother Lianbao was exempted from banishment punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his strategic skill and battlefield courage, directed that he be recommended whenever a Commandant-in-Chief post fell vacant, restored his yellow riding jacket and Baturu title, and remitted the banishment sentence on his younger brother Lianbao.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陳玉成、李侍賢合陷廬州、鳳陽，授勝保鑲黃旗蒙古都統，命為欽差大臣，督辦安徽軍務，連破賊於定遠池河、高橋。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels Chen Yucheng and Li Shixian together took Luzhou and Fengyang; Sheng Bao was appointed Mongol Commandant-in-Chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner, made Imperial Commissioner, and put in charge of Anhui military affairs; he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Dingyuan Chihe and Gaoqiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping generals Chen Yucheng and Li Shixian together seized Luzhou and Fengyang. Sheng Bao was made Mongol Commandant-in-Chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner, appointed Imperial Commissioner to oversee Anhui, and won successive victories at Dingyuan Chihe and Gaoqiao.

sentences.zh: 督軍抵三河，賊遁走。

translations.literal: Leading the army he reached Sanhe and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: He led his forces to Sanhe, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 捻首李兆受久踞江、淮間，與粵匪勾結。

translations.literal: The Nian chieftain Li Zhaoshou had long held the region between the Yangzi and Huai and colluded with Cantonese rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian leader Li Zhaoshou had long dominated the Yangzi–Huai region in collusion with the Taiping forces.

sentences.zh: 及見粵匪屢挫，漸持兩端。

translations.literal: When he saw the Cantonese rebels repeatedly defeated, he gradually wavered between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: As he watched the Taiping armies suffer repeated defeats, he began to hedge between the two sides.

sentences.zh: 勝保親至清流關密招之，許歸誠後免罪授官。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao personally went to Qingliuguan to recruit him in secret, promising that after surrender his crimes would be pardoned and he would receive an office.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao went in person to Qingliuguan to recruit him secretly, promising pardon and an official post if he submitted.

sentences.zh: 兆受以其部下家屬在江寧，請緩發。

translations.literal: Zhaoshou, because his subordinates' families were in Jiangning, asked to delay action.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshou asked to delay the rising because his men's families were still held in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 至是進攻天長，兆受內應，克之，遂獻滁州，奏授參將職，改名世忠，安置降★，自為一軍。

translations.literal: At this time he advanced to attack Tianchang; Zhaoshou responded from within; it was taken; he then offered Chuzhou; memorialized to grant the post of regimental colonel, changed his name to Shizhong, settled the surrendered followers, and formed his own army.
translations.idiomatic: When the attack on Tianchang began, Zhaoshou rose from within, the city fell, and he then surrendered Chuzhou. A memorial recommended him for regimental colonel, gave him the name Shizhong, settled his surrendered followers, and allowed him to keep a separate command.

sentences.zh: 九年，克六安，捻首張元龍以鳳陽降，复臨淮關。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he took Lu'an; the Nian chieftain Zhang Yuanlong surrendered Fengyang; Linhuai Pass was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he captured Lu'an; the Nian leader Zhang Yuanlong surrendered Fengyang; and Linhuai Pass was recovered.

sentences.zh: 進克霍山、盱眙，破賊清水鎮，斬其酋吳加孝，遂克懷遠，而廬州、定遠久未下，賊仍蔓延。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Huoshan and Xuyi, defeated the rebels at Qingshui Town, beheaded their chieftain Wu Jiaxiao, then took Huaiyuan; but Luzhou and Dingyuan long remained untaken and the rebels still spread.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to take Huoshan and Xuyi, routed the rebels at Qingshui Town and beheaded their leader Wu Jiaxiao, and then recovered Huaiyuan. Yet Luzhou and Dingyuan remained untaken for a long time, and rebel bands still spread across the province.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，奪情留軍。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; his grief was set aside and he remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was granted leave from mourning to remain at his post with the army.

sentences.zh: 十年，罷欽差大臣，命赴河南剿匪。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was removed as Imperial Commissioner and ordered to go to Henan to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was relieved as Imperial Commissioner and ordered to Henan to suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 御史林之望論劾，降授鑲藍旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Zhiwang memorialized in criticism; he was demoted and appointed Vice Commandant-in-Chief of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lin Zhiwang impeached him, and he was demoted to Vice Commandant-in-Chief of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 复坐剿匪不力，降授光祿寺卿，召回京。

translations.literal: Again, for ineffective bandit suppression, he was demoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for failing to suppress the bandits effectively, he was demoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 甫至，會英法聯軍內犯，命率八旗禁軍駐定福莊，偕僧格林沁、瑞麟進戰通州八里橋，敗績，勝保受傷，退保京師。

translations.literal: Hardly had he arrived when the Anglo-French allied armies invaded inland; he was ordered to lead the Eight Banner palace guards encamped at Dingfuzhuang, and together with Sengge Rinchen and Ruilin advanced to fight at Baliqiao in Tongzhou; they were defeated, Sheng Bao was wounded, and they fell back to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely arrived when the Anglo-French expedition advanced inland. He was ordered to lead the Eight Banner palace guards at Dingfuzhuang and, with Sengge Rinchen and Ruilin, to meet the enemy at Baliqiao near Tongzhou. They were defeated, Sheng Bao was wounded, and the army fell back to defend Beijing.

sentences.zh: 停戰議和，勝保收集各路潰軍及勤王師續至者共萬餘人。

translations.literal: When fighting ceased and peace was negotiated, Sheng Bao gathered routed troops from all routes and relief armies that continued to arrive, more than ten thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: After the truce and peace negotiations, Sheng Bao gathered routed troops from every column and relief forces still arriving, more than ten thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 疏陳京兵亟應訓練，擬議章程以進。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that capital troops urgently needed training and drafted regulations to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the capital garrison urgently needed training and submitted a draft set of regulations.

sentences.zh: 命兼管圓明園八旗、內務府包衣三旗，親督操練，是為改練京兵之始。

translations.literal: He was ordered concurrently to manage the Yuanmingyuan Eight Banners and the three bondservant banners of the Imperial Household Department, personally supervising drill—this was the beginning of reorganizing and training the capital troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take charge as well of the Yuanmingyuan Eight Banners and the three bondservant banners of the Imperial Household Department, personally supervising their drill—the beginning of the capital army's reorganization and training.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢兵部侍郎，捻匪擾山東，詔分所部五千人畀僧格林沁往剿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War; Nian bandits harassed Shandong, and an edict divided five thousand of his troops and gave them to Sengge Rinchen to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War. When Nian rebels ravaged Shandong, an edict detached five thousand of his men and placed them under Sengge Rinchen for the campaign there.

sentences.zh: 尋命勝保赴直、東交界治防，連克丘縣、館陶、冠縣、莘縣，破賊老巢。

translations.literal: Soon Sheng Bao was ordered to go to the Zhili–Shandong border to manage defense; he in succession took Qiu County, Guantao, Guan County, and Shen County, and destroyed the rebels' old lair.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to the Zhili–Shandong border to organize defenses, took Qiu County, Guantao, Guan County, and Shen County in succession, and destroyed the rebels' main stronghold.

sentences.zh: 招降捻首宋景詩，率眾隨軍。

translations.literal: He induced the Nian chieftain Song Jingshi to surrender, and Song led his followers with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He induced the Nian leader Song Jingshi to surrender, and Song marched with his followers in Sheng Bao's train.

sentences.zh: 复朝城、觀城，命督辦河南、安徽剿匪事宜。

translations.literal: He recovered Chaocheng and Guancheng and was ordered to supervise bandit suppression in Henan and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Chaocheng and Guancheng and was ordered to oversee bandit suppression in Henan and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 河北肅清，予優敘。

translations.literal: Hebei was pacified and he received preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: With Hebei pacified, he received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，文宗崩於行在，穆宗嗣位，肅順、載垣、端華等輔政專擅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year Emperor Wenzong died at the traveling palace; Emperor Muzong succeeded; Sushun, Zaiyuan, Duanhua, and others monopolized regency power.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year Emperor Wenzong died at the traveling palace and Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, while Sushun, Zaiyuan, Duanhua, and others seized exclusive control of the regency.

sentences.zh: 勝保昌言將入清君側，肅順等頗忌憚之。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao openly declared he would enter the capital to purge the emperor's side, and Sushun and the others were quite wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao openly declared that he would march on the capital to purge the emperor's inner circle, and Sushun and his allies were deeply wary of him.

sentences.zh: 洎回鑾，上疏曰：「政柄操之自上，非臣下所得專。

translations.literal: When the court returned to the capital he submitted a memorial saying: 'Political power is wielded from above; it is not for subjects to monopolize.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to Beijing he memorialized: 'Political authority belongs to the throne above; it is not something subjects may seize for themselves.

sentences.zh: 皇上沖齡嗣位，輔政得人，方足以資治理。

translations.literal: The emperor succeeded at a tender age; only with worthy regents can governance be supported.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty succeeded while still a child; only with the right regents can the realm be governed well.

sentences.zh: 怡親王載垣、鄭親王端華等非不宣力有年，赫赫師尹，民具爾瞻；

translations.literal: Prince Yi Zaiyuan, Prince Zheng Duanhua, and others have not failed to exert themselves for years; as illustrious ministers the people look up to them;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Zaiyuan, Prince Zheng Duanhua, and the others have served diligently for years and stand before the people as eminent ministers;

sentences.zh: 今竟攬君國大權，以臣僕而代綸音，挾至尊而令天下，實無以副寄託之望，而饜四海之心。

translations.literal: yet now they have seized the great power of ruler and state, substituting subjects' voices for the imperial edict, holding the supreme sovereign to command the realm—this truly cannot fulfill the hopes of entrustment or satisfy the hearts within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: yet they have now seized the great power of state, letting servants speak in place of the Son of Heaven and wielding the young emperor to command the empire. This cannot fulfill the late emperor's trust or satisfy the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 該王等以承寫硃諭為辭，居之不疑。

translations.literal: These princes take copying the vermilion rescript as their plea and occupy the position without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: These princes cite their commission to copy the late emperor's vermilion rescript and hold power without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 不知皇上纘承大統，天與人歸，原不以硃諭之有無為重。

translations.literal: They do not know that Your Majesty inherited the great succession—Heaven gave it and the people returned to you—and originally the presence or absence of a vermilion rescript was not what mattered.
translations.idiomatic: They forget that Your Majesty inherited the Mandate—granted by Heaven and affirmed by the people—and that the throne never depended on whether a vermilion rescript existed.

sentences.zh: 至贊襄政務，當以親親尊賢為斷，不當專以承寫為憑。

translations.literal: As for assisting in government, kin should be honored and the worthy respected—that should be the standard—not reliance solely on having copied the rescript.
translations.idiomatic: As for assisting in government, the standard should be honoring kin and respecting the worthy, not merely having been named to copy a rescript.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝彌留之際，近支親王多不在側。

translations.literal: When the late emperor was at his last breath, many close imperial princes were not at his side.
translations.idiomatic: At the late emperor's deathbed most of the close imperial princes were not present.

sentences.zh: 仰窺顧命苦衷，所以未留親筆硃諭者，未必非以輔政之難得其人，待皇上自擇而任之，以成未竟之志也。

translations.literal: Looking up to discern the anguish of the dying charge, the reason he left no vermilion rescript in his own hand was perhaps precisely because worthy regents are hard to find, waiting for Your Majesty to choose and appoint them yourself to complete the unfulfilled will.
translations.idiomatic: One may infer from the anguish of his final charge that he left no rescript in his own hand precisely because worthy regents are hard to find—leaving Your Majesty to choose and appoint them yourself and so fulfill his unfinished will.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖既未親政，皇太后又不臨朝，是政柄盡付之該王等數人。

translations.literal: The succeeding sage has not yet taken personal rule, and the empress dowager does not hold court; thus political power is entirely placed in the hands of these few princes.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor has not yet assumed personal rule, and the empress dowager does not hold court, so political power has passed entirely to these few princes.

sentences.zh: 其託諸掣籤簡放，鈐用符信圖章，以此取信於人，無如人皆不信，民碞可畏，天下難欺。

translations.literal: They entrust matters to drawing lots for appointments and applying seals and cipher marks, using these to win people's trust; yet people do not believe, the people's murmurs are to be feared, and the realm cannot be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: They rely on drawing lots for appointments and stamping documents with seals and cipher marks to win trust, yet no one believes them. Popular discontent is to be feared; the realm cannot be deceived.

sentences.zh: 近如御史董元醇條陳，極有關係，應準應駁，惟當斷自聖裁，廣集廷議，以定行止。

translations.literal: Recently, as with Censor Dong Yuanchun's submission, the matter is of the greatest relevance; whether to approve or reject should be decided solely by the sacred judgment, with broad court deliberation to fix the course of action.
translations.idiomatic: Take the recent submission of Censor Dong Yuanchun: it was a matter of the highest importance, to be approved or rejected only by Your Majesty's own judgment after full deliberation in court.

sentences.zh: 乃徑行擬旨駁斥，已開矯竊之端，大失臣民之望。

translations.literal: Yet they directly drafted an edict to reject it, already opening the breach of usurpation, and greatly disappointing officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they drafted and issued a rejection on their own authority, opening the door to usurpation and deeply disappointing officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 道路之人皆曰：'此非吾君之言也，非母后聖母之意也。

translations.literal: People on the road all say: 'These are not our ruler's words, nor the empress dowager's holy intent.
translations.idiomatic: People in the streets say: 'These are not our emperor's words, nor the empress dowager's will.

sentences.zh: '一切發號施令，真偽難分。

translations.literal: ' In all issuing of orders and commands, true and false are hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: ' With every order and command that goes forth, no one can tell what is genuine and what is not.

sentences.zh: 眾情洶洶，咸懷不服。

translations.literal: Popular feeling is turbulent; all harbor discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Public sentiment is in uproar, and everyone feels aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，宣宗成皇帝之天下，傳之文宗顯皇帝以付之我皇上者也。

translations.literal: The realm is the realm of Emperor Xuanzong Cheng, transmitted through Emperor Wenzong Xian to be entrusted to our present emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empire belongs to Emperor Xuanzong, passed down through Emperor Wenzong to our present sovereign.

sentences.zh: 昔我文皇后雖無垂簾之明文，而有聽政之實用。

translations.literal: Formerly our Empress Wen, though without explicit words of holding the curtain, had the practical effect of hearing government.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Empress Wen, though never formally said to 'hold the curtain behind the throne,' in practice governed from behind it.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，非皇太后親理萬幾，召對群臣，無以通下情而正國體；

translations.literal: For the present plan, unless the empress dowager personally handles the myriad affairs, summons and addresses the ministers, there is no way to convey lower sentiments and rectify the state's form;
translations.idiomatic: For the present, unless the empress dowager personally handles state affairs and receives the ministers in audience, there is no way to learn what the people feel or to set the polity right;

sentences.zh: 非特簡近支親王佐理庶政，盡心匡弼，無以振紀綱而順人心。

translations.literal: unless close imperial princes are specially selected to assist in ordinary government and devote themselves to support, there is no way to revive discipline and accord with people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: and unless close imperial princes are chosen to assist in government and give loyal counsel, there is no way to restore discipline or win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 惟有籥懇皇上俯察芻蕘，即奉皇太后權宜聽政，而於近支親王擇賢而任，仍秉命而行，以成郅治。

translations.literal: only if Your Majesty earnestly examines this humble counsel, immediately follows the empress dowager in provisional hearing of government, and among close imperial princes selects the worthy to appoint, still acting on command, can perfect order be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this humble advice: let the empress dowager provisionally hear government at once, choose worthy princes of the close line to assist, and let them still act only on your command, so that perfect order may be achieved.

sentences.zh: 」奏上，會大學士周祖培等亦以為言，下廷議，從之。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial was submitted, Grand Secretary Zhou Zupei and others also spoke likewise; it was sent for court deliberation and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the memorial was submitted, Grand Secretary Zhou Zupei and others made the same argument. The court deliberated and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 肅順等並伏法。

translations.literal: Sushun and the others were all executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Sushun and his associates were all executed.

sentences.zh: 尋授鑲黃旗滿洲都統兼正藍旗護軍統領。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Manchu Commandant-in-Chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner and concurrently Garrison Commander of the Plain Blue Banner guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Manchu Commandant-in-Chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner and concurrently commander of the Plain Blue Banner guards.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪肆擾皖、豫間，以張洛行為最強。

translations.literal: At the time Nian bandits rampaged between Anhui and Henan, with Zhang Luoxing the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Nian rebels ravaged the Anhui–Henan borderlands, and Zhang Luoxing was the strongest of their leaders.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖自踞壽州，逼走巡撫翁同書後，佯稱就撫，陰與粵匪陳玉成勾結。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin on his own seized Shouzhou; after driving away Governor Weng Tongshu he pretended to submit to pacification while secretly colluding with Cantonese rebel Chen Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Peilin had seized Shouzhou on his own authority and, after forcing out Governor Weng Tongshu, pretended to submit while secretly colluding with the Taiping general Chen Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 署巡撫賈臻被圍於潁州，久不解。

translations.literal: Acting Governor Jia Zhen was besieged at Yingzhou and for a long time the siege was not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Governor Jia Zhen was besieged at Yingzhou, and the siege dragged on without relief.

sentences.zh: 楚軍已克安慶，陳玉成退踞廬州。

translations.literal: The Chu army had already taken Anqing, and Chen Yucheng withdrew to hold Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan army had already captured Anqing, and Chen Yucheng had fallen back to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷本意安徽軍事屬之李續宜，用為巡撫。

translations.literal: The court's original intent was that Anhui military affairs belong to Li Xuyi, who was appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: The court had intended that Anhui operations be placed under Li Xuyi, who was appointed governor.

sentences.zh: 沛霖舊隸勝保部下，心憚楚軍，揚言勝保來始薙發。

translations.literal: Peilin had formerly been under Sheng Bao's command; in his heart he feared the Chu army and proclaimed that only when Sheng Bao came would he shave his head in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin had once served under Sheng Bao. He feared the Hunan army and declared that he would shave his head and submit only when Sheng Bao arrived.

sentences.zh: 賈臻以聞，詔促勝保援潁州。

translations.literal: Jia Zhen reported this, and an edict urged Sheng Bao to relieve Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhen reported the situation, and an edict ordered Sheng Bao to hurry to the relief of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，遣軍先進，為賊所挫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he sent troops forward first, and they were defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he sent an advance force ahead, and it was beaten by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 三月，勝保至，擊破賊壘，圍乃解，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the third month Sheng Bao arrived, attacked and broke the rebel stockades, and the siege was lifted; he was given the rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Sheng Bao arrived, stormed the rebel camps, and lifted the siege. He was given the rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿等克廬州，陳玉成遁走，沛霖誘擒之，獻於勝保軍。

translations.literal: Duolong'a and others took Luzhou; Chen Yucheng fled; Peilin lured and captured him and presented him to Sheng Bao's army.
translations.idiomatic: Duolong'a and others captured Luzhou. Chen Yucheng fled, but Peilin lured him into capture and delivered him to Sheng Bao's camp.

sentences.zh: 詔於軍前誅玉成，赦沛霖罪，許立功後復官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yucheng executed before the army; Peilin's crimes were pardoned, and he was permitted to recover his office after meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chen Yucheng executed before the army, pardoned Peilin, and promised restoration of his rank if he rendered meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 沛霖擁眾號十萬，所屬二百餘圩。

translations.literal: Peilin commanded forces said to number one hundred thousand, with more than two hundred stockaded villages under him.
translations.idiomatic: Peilin commanded a force said to number one hundred thousand men across more than two hundred fortified villages.

sentences.zh: 與張洛行勢敵相仇，自請剿之，心實叵測。

translations.literal: He was a match in power and an enemy of Zhang Luoxing; he volunteered to suppress him, but his heart was truly hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: He was Zhang Luoxing's equal in strength and his bitter enemy, and he volunteered to suppress him—yet his true intentions were impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 詔詢曾國籓、官文、李續宜、袁甲三等，皆主剿。

translations.literal: The throne inquired of Zeng Guofan, Guanwen, Li Xuyi, Yuan Jiasan, and others; all advocated suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The court consulted Zeng Guofan, Guanwen, Li Xuyi, Yuan Jiasan, and others; all favored suppressing Peilin by force.

sentences.zh: 獨勝保一意主撫，上疏言事權不一，身為客軍，地方掣肘，請以安徽、河南兩巡撫幫辦軍務，允之。

translations.literal: Only Sheng Bao insisted solely on pacification; he memorialized that authority was not unified, that as a guest army he was checked by local officials, and requested that the governors of Anhui and Henan assist in military affairs; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao alone insisted on pacification. He memorialized that command authority was fragmented, that as an outside army he was hamstrung by local officials, and asked that the governors of Anhui and Henan be ordered to assist him; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 迭詔訓飭，褒其才略，戒其驕愎。

translations.literal: Edicts repeatedly admonished him, praising his talent and strategy while warning against arrogance and obstinacy.
translations.idiomatic: Edict after edict admonished him, praising his ability while warning him against arrogance and obstinacy.

sentences.zh: 卒不悛，力言沛霖無他，而為李續宜所疑，恐激變。

translations.literal: In the end he did not reform; he strongly asserted Peilin had no other intent, but Li Xuyi suspected him and feared provoking a revolt.
translations.idiomatic: He never mended his ways, insisting that Peilin meant no harm, while Li Xuyi distrusted Peilin and feared provoking an uprising.

sentences.zh: 續宜奉旨進駐潁州，亦迄不至。

translations.literal: Xuyi was ordered by edict to advance and encamp at Yingzhou, yet in the end he never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuyi was ordered to advance and take post at Yingzhou, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 會陝西回亂熾，多隆阿援軍阻隔不能遽達。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Muslim rebellion in Shaanxi flared fiercely; Duolong'a's relief army was blocked and could not arrive quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Muslim uprising in Shaanxi grew fierce, and Duolong'a's relief column was blocked and could not reach the province quickly.

sentences.zh: 遂授勝保欽差大臣，督辦陝西軍務。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao was then appointed Imperial Commissioner to supervise Shaanxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao was then appointed Imperial Commissioner to oversee military affairs in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 八月，轉戰至西安，解其圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he fought in succession to Xi'an and lifted its siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he fought his way to Xi'an and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 降捻宋景詩中途率眾叛走。

translations.literal: The surrendered Nian Song Jingshi midway led his followers in revolt and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered Nian leader Song Jingshi rebelled en route and fled with his followers.

sentences.zh: 東路同州、朝邑猶為回踞，詔責勝保專剿東路，命多隆阿進軍分任西路。

translations.literal: On the eastern route Tongzhou and Chaoyi were still held by Muslims; an edict charged Sheng Bao solely with suppressing the eastern route and ordered Duolong'a to advance and take the western route separately.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern front Tongzhou and Chaoyi were still in rebel hands. An edict made Sheng Bao responsible for the eastern campaign and ordered Duolong'a to take the western front.

sentences.zh: 勝保力不能制賊，而忌多隆阿，擅調苗沛霖率兵赴陝，嚴詔斥阻，不聽。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao lacked the strength to control the rebels yet envied Duolong'a; on his own authority he transferred Miao Peilin to lead troops to Shaanxi; stern edicts rebuked and blocked this, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao could not master the rebels yet resented Duolong'a. On his own authority he ordered Miao Peilin to march into Shaanxi; stern edicts forbade it, but he refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 命僧格林沁大軍監製，乃止。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen's great army was ordered to supervise and restrain him, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Sengge Rinchen's main force was ordered to restrain him did he desist.

sentences.zh: 於是中外交章劾勝保驕縱貪婬，冒餉納賄，擁兵縱寇，欺罔貽誤，下僧格林沁及山西巡撫英桂、西安副都統德興阿察實奏上，密詔多隆阿率師至陝，傳旨宣布勝保罪狀，褫職逮京，交刑部治罪，籍其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chinese and foreign officials alike memorialized impeaching Sheng Bao for arrogance, indulgence, greed, and lust, embezzling pay and taking bribes, holding troops while letting bandits go, deceiving and causing delay; Sengge Rinchen and Shanxi Governor Yinggui and Xi'an Vice Commandant De Xing'a were ordered to investigate and report facts; a secret edict ordered Duolong'a to lead troops to Shaanxi, proclaim Sheng Bao's crimes, strip his office, arrest him to the capital, hand him to the Ministry of Punishments for trial, and confiscate his household property.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials then poured in from every quarter impeaching Sheng Bao for arrogance, debauchery, embezzlement, bribery, keeping troops idle while rebels roamed free, and deceiving the throne. Sengge Rinchen, Shanxi Governor Yinggui, and Xi'an Vice Commandant De Xing'a were ordered to investigate and report. A secret edict sent Duolong'a into Shaanxi to proclaim Sheng Bao's crimes, strip him of office, bring him to the capital for trial by the Ministry of Punishments, and confiscate his property.

sentences.zh: 二年，王大臣會鞫，勝保僅自承攜妾隨營，呈訴參劾諸人誣告之罪。

translations.literal: In the second year princes and ministers jointly tried him; Sheng Bao admitted only that he had brought a concubine with the camp and presented a plea that those who impeached him had falsely accused him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a joint tribunal of princes and ministers tried him. Sheng Bao admitted only to bringing a concubine on campaign and pleaded that his accusers had slandered him.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其貪污欺罔，天下共知，苗沛霖已戕官踞城，宋景詩反覆背叛，皆其養筴貽患，不得謂無挾制朝廷之意；

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him: his corruption and deception are known throughout the realm; Miao Peilin has already killed officials and seized cities, Song Jingshi has repeatedly betrayed—all disasters he nurtured and fostered; one cannot say he had no intent to hold the court hostage;
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him: his corruption and deceit were known to all. Miao Peilin had murdered officials and seized cities; Song Jingshi had betrayed the court again and again—troubles he himself had nurtured. He could not be said free of intent to coerce the throne;

sentences.zh: 念其戰功足錄，從寬賜自盡，並逮其從官論罪有差。

translations.literal: considering his battle achievements sufficient to record, he was leniently granted suicide by his own hand, and his attendant officials were also arrested and punished in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: yet in consideration of his past victories he was granted the lenient sentence of suicide, and his subordinate officers were arrested and punished according to their degrees of guilt.

sentences.zh: 當其被逮也，降捻李世忠已擢至提督，請黜己官為之贖罪，不許。

translations.literal: When he was arrested, the surrendered Nian Li Shizhong had already been promoted to regional commander and asked to demote himself to redeem Sheng Bao's crime; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of his arrest the surrendered Nian leader Li Shizhong, by then a regional commander, asked to give up his own rank to redeem him; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 御史吳台壽疏言勝保有克敵禦侮之功，無失地喪師之罪，請從末減。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Taishou memorialized that Sheng Bao had the achievement of defeating enemies and repelling insult, had no crime of losing territory or armies, and asked that the penalty be reduced to the least.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Taishou memorialized that Sheng Bao had defeated enemies and defended the realm, had never lost territory or squandered an army, and asked that the sentence be reduced.

sentences.zh: 台壽兄台朗在勝保軍中，詔斥黨附，褫台壽職。

translations.literal: Taishou's elder brother Tailang was in Sheng Bao's army; an edict rebuked factional attachment and stripped Taishou of office.
translations.idiomatic: Taishou's elder brother Tailang had served in Sheng Bao's army. An edict denounced the memorial as partisan favoritism and stripped Taishou of his post.

sentences.zh: 托明阿，棟鄂氏，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 由侍衛擢護軍參領，出為山東兗州營游擊。

translations.literal: From bodyguard he was promoted to company commander of the guards, then went out as brigade commander of the Yanzhou garrison in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from the imperial bodyguard to a guards company command, he was then posted as brigade commander of the Yanzhou garrison in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 從巡撫武隆阿徵回疆，以功賜花翎。

translations.literal: He followed Governor Wulong'a in the campaign in the Western Regions and for merit was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in the Western Regions under Governor Wulong'a and was awarded the peacock feather for his service.

sentences.zh: 累擢曹州鎮總兵，調四川松潘、重慶二鎮。

translations.literal: By successive promotions he became regional commander of Caozhou garrison, then was transferred to the Songpan and Chongqing garrisons in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to regional commander of the Caozhou garrison and was later transferred to command the Songpan and Chongqing garrisons in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年，擢四川提督，以病去職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Sichuan provincial military commander and left office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang he was made provincial military commander of Sichuan, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，起授烏魯木齊提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was recalled and appointed provincial military commander of Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was recalled to service as provincial military commander of Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 調陝西，擢綏遠城將軍，整飭戎政，勤於訓練。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shaanxi, he was promoted to General of Suiyuan City, put military administration in order, and was diligent in training.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shaanxi, he was promoted to General of Suiyuan and set about restoring military discipline with tireless attention to drill.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪林鳳祥等陷揚州，逼淮、徐，命率所部赴江南、山東交界防堵，進屯清江浦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Cantonese rebels Lin Fengxiang and others took Yangzhou and pressed Huai and Xu; he was ordered to lead his troops to the Jiangnan–Shandong border for defense and encamped at Qingjiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng the Taiping generals Lin Fengxiang and others seized Yangzhou and threatened the Huai and Xu regions. Tuo Ming'a was ordered to the Jiangnan–Shandong border with his troops and encamped at Qingjiangpu.

sentences.zh: 賊竄滁州，托明阿赴援，與週天爵會剿。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Chuzhou; Tuo Ming'a went to relieve it and joined Zhou Tianjue in joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels moved on Chuzhou, Tuo Ming'a marched to its relief and joined Zhou Tianjue in a combined campaign.

sentences.zh: 遂追賊至河南，迭戰於睢州、杞縣、陳留、中牟，進克汜水，殲賊千餘，被珍賚，命襄辦軍務。

translations.literal: He then pursued the rebels into Henan, fought repeatedly at Suizhou, Qi County, Chenliu, and Zhongmou, advanced and took Sishui, annihilated more than a thousand rebels, received imperial rewards, and was ordered to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels into Henan and fought successive engagements at Suizhou, Qi County, Chenliu, and Zhongmou before taking Sishui and killing more than a thousand rebels. He received imperial rewards and was ordered to assist in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊竄河北，圍懷慶，乃渡河會諸軍分路進攻，迭有斬獲。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Hebei and besieged Huaiqing; he then crossed the river, joined the armies, and attacked on separate routes with repeated kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke into Hebei and besieged Huaiqing. He crossed the river, joined the allied armies in a multi-pronged assault, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 賊築土城樹木柵以拒，合攻破之，擒斬數千。

translations.literal: The rebels built earthen walls and planted wooden palisades to resist; the combined forces broke them and captured and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw up earthen walls and wooden palisades to hold them off; the allied forces stormed the works and killed or captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊始遁，懷慶圍解。

translations.literal: The rebels at last fled and the siege of Huaiqing was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels finally fled, and the siege of Huaiqing was lifted.

sentences.zh: 論功，賜黃馬褂，予西林巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the yellow riding jacket and given the title Xilin Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: For his merits he was awarded the yellow riding jacket and the title Xilin Baturu.

sentences.zh: 追賊山西，詔以勝保督師，命托明阿襄辦。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels into Shanxi, an edict placed Sheng Bao in command and ordered Tuo Ming'a to assist.
translations.idiomatic: As the pursuit continued into Shanxi, an edict made Sheng Bao supreme commander and ordered Tuo Ming'a to assist him.

sentences.zh: 賊竄入直隸境，坐降五級留任，尋以傷劇解職回旗。

translations.literal: When the rebels fled into Zhili territory he was demoted five ranks but retained his post; soon, because his wounds were severe, he was relieved and returned to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels broke into Zhili he was demoted five ranks but kept his post; soon afterward, his wounds being grave, he was relieved and sent back to his banner.

sentences.zh: 四年春，病痊，命赴直隸，仍幫辦僧格林沁、勝保軍務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, his illness cured, he was ordered to Zhili and again assisted in the military affairs of Sengge Rinchen and Sheng Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, recovered from illness, he was ordered to Zhili to assist again in the campaigns of Sengge Rinchen and Sheng Bao.

sentences.zh: 賊方踞阜城，堅守不出，諸軍圍之。

translations.literal: The rebels were then holding Fucheng, defending stubbornly without coming out, and the armies besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were holding Fucheng, refusing to come out, while the allied armies tightened the siege around them.

sentences.zh: 托明阿屯東北，賊來撲，輒擊退，突由東南隅竄出，踞連鎮，夾運河。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a encamped on the northeast; when rebels came to attack he always beat them back; they suddenly broke out from the southeast corner, seized Lianzhen, and straddled the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a held the northeast sector and repelled every rebel assault, but the enemy suddenly broke out from the southeast, seized Lianzhen, and straddled the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 托明阿與都統西凌阿軍東西兩岸，圍復合。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a and Commandant-in-Chief Xiling'a had armies on the eastern and western banks, and the encirclement closed again.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a and Commandant-in-Chief Xiling'a took the eastern and western banks of the canal, and the encirclement was restored.

sentences.zh: 會琦善督師揚州，卒於軍，命托明阿為欽差大臣，馳往代之，授江寧將軍。

translations.literal: When Qishan was commanding at Yangzhou he died in camp; Tuo Ming'a was appointed Imperial Commissioner, ordered to hurry and replace him, and made General of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan, who had been commanding at Yangzhou, died in camp. Tuo Ming'a was appointed Imperial Commissioner, ordered posthaste to replace him, and made General of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 自賊踞江寧，鎮江、揚州皆陷，南北梗阻，大軍分兩路，向榮軍江南，琦善軍江北。

translations.literal: Since the rebels held Jiangning, Zhenjiang and Yangzhou had both fallen, north and south were blocked; the great armies divided into two routes—Xiang Rong's army in Jiangnan, Qishan's in Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the rebels seized Jiangning, Zhenjiang and Yangzhou had fallen and communications between north and south were cut. The main forces were divided: Xiang Rong's army in Jiangnan and Qishan's in Jiangbei.

sentences.zh: 江北軍攻揚州不能克，賊棄城去，聚於瓜洲，與南岸鎮江相犄角。

translations.literal: The Jiangbei army attacked Yangzhou but could not take it; the rebels abandoned the city, gathered at Guazhou, and with Zhenjiang on the south bank formed a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbei army failed to retake Yangzhou. The rebels abandoned the city, massed at Guazhou, and with Zhenjiang on the opposite bank formed a mutually supporting pair of strongholds.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊時乘鉅簰順流而下，陸師不能扼，水師力薄，亦不能制賊。

translations.literal: Jiangning rebels at times rode great rafts downstream; the land army could not block them, the naval force was weak, and could not control the rebels either.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces from Jiangning often swept downstream on great rafts. The land army could not stop them, and the navy, being too weak, could not bring them to heel either.

sentences.zh: 上游浦口最當衝要，賊於沙洲結營，時圖進竄。

translations.literal: Upstream, Pukou was the most critical point; the rebels encamped on sandbars and from time to time sought to break through.
translations.idiomatic: Farther upstream, Pukou was the most critical point. The rebels camped on the sandbars and repeatedly tried to break through.

sentences.zh: 恃總兵武慶一軍及道員溫紹原六合練勇為屏蔽，亦不能進取。

translations.literal: Relying on Regional Commander Wu Qing's army and Intendant Wen Shaoyuan's Liuhe militia as a screen, they still could not advance and take ground.
translations.idiomatic: Even with Regional Commander Wu Qing's force and Intendant Wen Shaoyuan's Liuhe militia as a screen, government troops still could not advance.

sentences.zh: 托明阿至軍，令副將鞠殿華毀運河鐵钅巢，提督陳金綬循東岸進攻，小有斬獲。

translations.literal: When Tuo Ming'a reached the army he ordered Deputy General Ju Dianhua to destroy the iron barriers on the canal; Regional Commander Chen Jinshou advanced along the eastern bank and had minor kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuo Ming'a took command he ordered Deputy General Ju Dianhua to clear the iron barriers from the canal and had Regional Commander Chen Jinshou attack along the eastern bank, winning minor successes.

sentences.zh: 又截擊賊簰，斃偽丞相黃起茅。

translations.literal: He also intercepted rebel rafts and killed the false chancellor Huang Qimao.
translations.idiomatic: He also intercepted rebel rafts and killed the false chancellor Huang Qimao.

sentences.zh: 自督舟師渡江，略北固山、金山而還。

translations.literal: He personally led the fleet across the river, raided Beigu Hill and Jinshan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led the fleet across the Yangzi, raided Beigu Hill and Jinshan, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年，瓜洲、鎮江賊合犯儀徵，令副都統德興阿、總兵李志和擊退。

translations.literal: In the fifth year rebels from Guazhou and Zhenjiang jointly attacked Yizheng; he ordered Vice Commandant De Xing'a and Regional Commander Li Zhihe to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year rebels from Guazhou and Zhenjiang jointly attacked Yizheng. He ordered Vice Commandant De Xing'a and Regional Commander Li Zhihe to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 又進軍三汊河，誘賊敗之。

translations.literal: He again advanced to Sanhe River, lured the rebels, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced again to Sancha River, lured the rebels into an ambush, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 托明阿見僧格林沁於連鎮、馮官屯皆以圍牆制賊，議仿其法，於瓜洲築長圍以困之。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a saw that at Lianzhen and Fengguantun Sengge Rinchen had all used encircling walls to control rebels; he proposed imitating the method and building a long encirclement at Guazhou to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Sengge Rinchen had contained rebels at Lianzhen and Fengguantun with encircling walls, Tuo Ming'a proposed the same method at Guazhou and began building a long cordon to starve the enemy out.

sentences.zh: 然瓜洲濱大江，江路不斷，且地勢袤長不易守，實無足恃。

translations.literal: Yet Guazhou bordered the great river, the river route was unbroken, and the terrain was long and hard to defend—truly not something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guazhou lay on the great river, the water route remained open, and the ground was too extended to defend easily—the plan was fundamentally unsound.

sentences.zh: 圍成，屢偕陳金綬進攻，無大勝利。

translations.literal: When the encirclement was complete he repeatedly joined Chen Jinshou in attacks but won no great victories.
translations.idiomatic: When the cordon was finished he attacked again and again with Chen Jinshou but won no decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊踞江浦石磯橋，武慶​​、西昌阿等馳擊，克之。

translations.literal: Jiangning rebels held Shiji Bridge at Jiangpu; Wu Qing, Xichang'a, and others galloped to attack and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Jiangning held Shiji Bridge at Jiangpu until Wu Qing, Xichang'a, and others stormed it and recovered the position.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吉爾杭阿督師攻鎮江甚急，於是議南北同時進剿。

translations.literal: Governor Jirhang'a was pressing the attack on Zhenjiang with great urgency; thereupon they deliberated on simultaneous north–south advance to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jirhang'a was pressing the assault on Zhenjiang with great urgency, and the commanders resolved on a coordinated north–south offensive.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，江寧賊大舉援鎮江，未得逞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Jiangning rebels came in force to relieve Zhenjiang but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year a large rebel force from Jiangning marched to relieve Zhenjiang but failed.

sentences.zh: 渡江與瓜洲賊合，突越土圍，四出縱火。

translations.literal: They crossed the river, joined the Guazhou rebels, suddenly broke over the earthen encirclement, and set fires in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the river, united with the Guazhou garrison, broke through the earthen cordon, and set fires on every side.

sentences.zh: 官軍戰土橋竟日，傷亡多​​。

translations.literal: Government troops fought at Tuqiao all day with many casualties.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops fought at Tuqiao all day and suffered heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 托明阿營壘被毀，退三汊河，又退秦家橋，幾不能軍。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a's camps were destroyed; he retreated to Sanhe River, then again to Qinjia Bridge, and nearly could not keep an army together.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a's camps were overrun. He fell back to Sancha River, then to Qinjia Bridge, and his army was nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 陳金綬、雷以諴等亦退走，揚州遂陷。

translations.literal: Chen Jinshou, Lei Yixian, and others also retreated, and Yangzhou then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jinshou, Lei Yixian, and others also fled, and Yangzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 諸營潰散，惟德興阿猶整軍力戰。

translations.literal: The various camps collapsed and scattered; only De Xing'a still kept his army in order and fought hard.
translations.idiomatic: The camps collapsed in rout; only De Xing'a kept his force intact and fought on.

sentences.zh: 向榮遣鄧紹良渡江來援。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong sent Deng Shaoliang across the river to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong sent Deng Shaoliang across the river with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 越十日，复揚州，而江浦亦為賊踞。

translations.literal: After ten days Yangzhou was recovered, but Jiangpu was also seized by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Yangzhou was recovered, but Jiangpu had in turn fallen to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 詔褫托明阿職，留營效力，尋以病歸。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Tuo Ming'a of office but left him in camp to serve; soon he returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Tuo Ming'a of rank but allowed him to remain with the army. He soon went home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 八年，予頭等侍衛，率兵駐楊村防英兵內犯，授直隸提督，遷西安將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made a first-class bodyguard, led troops encamped at Yangcun to guard against British invasion inland, was appointed Zhili provincial military commander, and transferred to General of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made a first-class bodyguard, stationed troops at Yangcun to guard against a British advance inland, was appointed provincial military commander of Zhili, and later transferred to General of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以傷病乞休，四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he requested retirement on grounds of wounds and illness; in the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he retired on grounds of wounds and illness, and died in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 陳金綬，四川岳池人。

translations.literal: Chen Jinshou was a native of Yuechi in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jinshou was a native of Yuechi in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 從剿教匪，授把總，積功至都司。

translations.literal: He followed in suppressing sectarian rebels, was appointed platoon commander, and by accumulated merit rose to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the campaigns against sectarian rebels, was made platoon commander, and rose by accumulated merit to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 道光初，從征回疆，破賊於佳噶賴，功最，賜號逸勇巴圖魯，擢留壩營游擊。

translations.literal: In the early Daoguang reign he campaigned in the Western Regions, defeated rebels at Jiagalai with the greatest merit, was granted the title Yiyong Baturu, and was promoted to brigade commander of the Liuba garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he campaigned in the Western Regions, won the decisive victory at Jiagalai, was granted the title Yiyong Baturu, and was promoted to brigade commander of the Liuba garrison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，直隸總督琦善調司教練，累擢督標中軍副將，琦善倚之，以堪勝總兵薦，擢天津鎮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhili Governor-General Qishan transferred him to supervise training; by successive promotions he became deputy commander of the governor-general's central army; Qishan relied on him and recommended him as fit for regional command; he was promoted to the Tianjin garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhili Governor-General Qishan put him in charge of drill. He rose to deputy commander of the governor-general's central brigade, and Qishan, relying on him heavily, recommended him for regional command and had him promoted to the Tianjin garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢直隸提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Zhili provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made provincial military commander of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 及琦善督師剿粵匪，率所部三千以從。

translations.literal: When Qishan commanded the army to suppress Cantonese rebels, he led his three thousand troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Qishan took command against the Taiping rebels, Chen Jinshou marched with three thousand of his own men.

sentences.zh: 詔金綬為楊遇春舊部，命幫辦軍務，率兵先發。

translations.literal: An edict noted that Jinshou was an old subordinate of Yang Yuchun, ordered him to assist in military affairs, and directed him to lead troops out first.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Jinshou had served under Yang Yuchun, ordered him to assist in the campaign, and directed him to march ahead with the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又以其不諳文字，命勝保偕行。

translations.literal: Also, because he was not versed in written documents, Sheng Bao was ordered to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was not literate in written Chinese, Sheng Bao was ordered to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年春，趣援江寧，偕勝保克浦口，詔責專防江北。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Xianfeng he was urged to relieve Jiangning; together with Sheng Bao he took Pukou; an edict charged him solely with defending Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Xianfeng he was ordered to hurry to the relief of Jiangning. With Sheng Bao he recovered Pukou, and an edict made him solely responsible for the defense of Jiangbei.

sentences.zh: 揚州陷，由六合、儀徵趨援。

translations.literal: When Yangzhou fell he hurried to relieve it by way of Liuhe and Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou fell he marched to its relief by way of Liuhe and Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 琦善大軍始至，合攻揚州。

translations.literal: Qishan's great army had only just arrived, and they jointly attacked Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan's main force had only just arrived when they launched a combined assault on Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 琦善軍其北，金綬、勝保軍其西，累戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Qishan's army was on the north, Jinshou's and Sheng Bao's on the west, and in repeated battles all were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan held the northern sector and Jinshou and Sheng Bao the western, and they won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 賊堅守數月不下，而瓜洲一路通江，兵少不能合圍。

translations.literal: The rebels held firm for months without being taken, yet the Guazhou route opened on the river, and with too few troops they could not complete the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held out for months, but the Guazhou line remained open to the river, and government forces were too few to close the ring completely.

sentences.zh: 賊分犯浦口踞之，進陷滁州，遂北竄。

translations.literal: The rebels divided forces, attacked and seized Pukou, advanced and took Chuzhou, then fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels split their force, seized Pukou, pushed on to take Chuzhou, and then bolted northward.

sentences.zh: 勝保率兵赴安徽應援，迭詔以孤城久抗，責攻益急。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao led troops to Anhui in relief; edicts repeatedly noted the lone city's long resistance and charged that attacks grow ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao marched to Anhui with reinforcements, while edict after edict rebuked the commanders for letting a single city resist so long and ordered fiercer assaults.

sentences.zh: 總兵雙來奮進，緣梯登城，金綬策應。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Shuang Lai pressed forward boldly, climbed the wall by ladder, and Jinshou coordinated in support.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Shuang Lai led a bold assault up scaling ladders while Jinshou coordinated the supporting attack.

sentences.zh: 兵不聽命，雙來以無援負創退，尋歿於軍，自此不敢力攻，而賊時由瓜洲窺伺來援，屢卻之。

translations.literal: The troops would not obey orders; Shuang Lai, lacking relief and wounded, withdrew, and soon died in camp; from then on they dared not attack with full force, while rebels from time to time watched from Guazhou for relief forces and were repeatedly repelled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops refused to follow orders. Shuang Lai, unsupported and wounded, fell back and soon died in camp. Thereafter the army dared not press a full assault, though rebel relief columns probing from Guazhou were turned back again and again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊陷儀徵，兩路同時來犯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the rebels took Yizheng and attacked on two routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebels captured Yizheng and attacked on two fronts at once.

sentences.zh: 參將馮景尼守楊子橋，先潰，諸軍多失利。

translations.literal: Regimental Commander Feng Jingni defended Yangzi Bridge but collapsed first; many armies suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental Commander Feng Jingni, defending Yangzi Bridge, broke first, and most of the government columns were beaten.

sentences.zh: 城賊擁輜重突出趨瓜洲，琦善、金綬不能截擊，並坐褫職留軍。

translations.literal: The city rebels, laden with baggage, broke out toward Guazhou; Qishan and Jinshou could not intercept them and both were stripped of office but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The city's defenders broke out with their baggage train toward Guazhou. Qishan and Jinshou failed to cut them off and were both stripped of rank but left with the army.

sentences.zh: 揚州雖復，賊久踞瓜洲。

translations.literal: Although Yangzhou was recovered, the rebels long held Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou was recovered, but the rebels continued to hold Guazhou for a long time.

sentences.zh: 四年春，琦善卒於軍，金綬暫署關防。
