translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year Qishan died in camp and Jinshou temporarily held the seal of command.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year Qishan died in camp, and Jinshou temporarily assumed command.

sentences.zh: 托明阿至，偕金綬進攻瓜洲，毀賊砲台。

translations.literal: When Tuo Ming'a arrived he joined Jinshou in attacking Guazhou and destroyed the rebel batteries.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuo Ming'a arrived he joined Jinshou in an assault on Guazhou and destroyed the rebel batteries.

sentences.zh: 尋攻新橋賊壘，金綬之侄能義及游擊海明殞於陣。

translations.literal: Soon they attacked the rebel stockade at Xinqiao; Jinshou's nephew Nengyi and Brigade Commander Haiming were killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They soon assaulted the rebel camp at Xinqiao, where Jinshou's nephew Nengyi and Brigade Commander Haiming were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 江北軍多疲玩，金綬年老，文宗以其謹願，姑容之。

translations.literal: The Jiangbei army was largely slack and indulgent; Jinshou was old; Emperor Wenzong, because of his cautious willingness, for the time being tolerated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbei army had grown slack. Jinshou was elderly, and Emperor Wenzong, valuing his dutiful character, for the time being indulged him.

sentences.zh: 閱時輒報小捷，屢以虛飾被斥。

translations.literal: From time to time he reported minor victories and was repeatedly rebuked for false embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: He reported minor victories from time to time and was repeatedly rebuked for inflating his reports.

sentences.zh: 至托明阿兵潰土橋，金綬及雷以諴駐萬福橋，望風而走。

translations.literal: When Tuo Ming'a's army was routed at Tuqiao, Jinshou and Lei Yixian, encamped at Wanfu Bridge, fled at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuo Ming'a's army was routed at Tuqiao, Jinshou and Lei Yixian, posted at Wanfu Bridge, fled at the first sign of defeat.

sentences.zh: 事後飾辭自辨，又奏隨同克復揚州，為德興阿論劾，應治罪，金綬已先歿於軍矣。

translations.literal: Afterward he embellished his words in self-defense and also memorialized that he had joined in recovering Yangzhou; De Xing'a memorialized in criticism that he should be punished; Jinshou had already died in camp beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he dressed up his account in self-defense and claimed to have helped recover Yangzhou. De Xing'a impeached him as deserving punishment, but Jinshou had already died in camp.

sentences.zh: 德興阿，喬佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人，黑龍江駐防。

translations.literal: De Xing'a, of the Qiaojia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, garrisoned in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a, of the Qiaojia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner from the Heilongjiang garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光末，由駐京前鋒授藍翎侍衛、乾清門行走，累擢頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign, from a vanguard stationed in the capital he was made a Blue Feather Bodyguard and attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and by successive promotions became a first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daoguang reign he rose from a capital-stationed vanguard to Blue Feather Bodyguard and attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and by stages to first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 以善​​騎射受文宗知，曾手擒奔馬，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: For skill in riding and archery he won Emperor Wenzong's notice; he once seized a runaway horse with his own hands and was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: His skill in riding and archery won Emperor Wenzong's favor. He once seized a runaway horse with his bare hands and was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，命率黑龍江兵赴琦善軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was ordered to lead Heilongjiang troops to Qishan's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was ordered to bring Heilongjiang troops to Qishan's command.

sentences.zh: 三年，從攻揚州，屯蔣家廟，為通儀徵要路，城賊竄出，奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in the attack on Yangzhou, encamped at Jiangjiamiao—the key route to Yizheng—defeated city rebels who broke out in a fierce attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined the assault on Yangzhou and encamped at Jiangjiamiao, the vital route to Yizheng, where he routed rebels breaking out of the city.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲援賊進踞虹橋，與守備毛三元夾擊於三汊河。

translations.literal: Guazhou relief rebels advanced and seized Hongqiao; together with Garrison Commander Mao Sanyuan he attacked from both sides at Sanhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements from Guazhou seized Hongqiao. He and Garrison Commander Mao Sanyuan caught them in a pincer at Sancha River.

sentences.zh: 德興阿單騎陷陣，射殪其酋，大破賊，加副都統銜。

translations.literal: De Xing'a alone on horseback plunged into the battle line, shot and killed their chieftain, inflicted a great defeat on the rebels, and was given the rank of Vice Commandant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a charged alone into the enemy ranks, shot down their leader, and won a crushing victory. He was given the rank of Vice Commandant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 別賊破儀徵，分兩路來犯。

translations.literal: Another rebel force took Yizheng and attacked on two routes.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel column captured Yizheng and attacked on two fronts.

sentences.zh: 德興阿急趨東石人頭，毀賊浮橋。

translations.literal: De Xing'a hurried to East Shirentou and destroyed the rebels' pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a rushed to East Shirentou and destroyed the rebels' pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 而瓜洲賊又進築土城於河西，偪三汊河，與儀徵賊相犄角。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Guazhou rebels again advanced and built earthen walls west of the river, pressing on Sanhe River and forming a pincer with the Yizheng rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Guazhou garrison threw up earthen walls on the west bank, pressed toward Sancha River, and linked with the Yizheng force in a mutually supporting position.

sentences.zh: 德興阿偕總兵瞿騰龍渡河毀賊營，賊乃不能西進。

translations.literal: De Xing'a together with Regional Commander Qu Tenglong crossed the river and destroyed rebel camps, so the rebels could not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a and Regional Commander Qu Tenglong crossed the river, destroyed the rebel camps, and blocked any further westward advance.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊棄揚州城退踞瓜洲，官軍進复儀徵，授正白旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels abandoned Yangzhou city and withdrew to hold Guazhou; government troops advanced and recovered Yizheng; he was appointed Vice Commandant-in-Chief of the Han Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels abandoned Yangzhou and fell back on Guazhou. Government troops recovered Yizheng, and he was made Vice Commandant-in-Chief of the Han Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 四年，偕瞿騰龍進攻瓜洲，騰龍深入，為賊所襲，殞於陣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, together with Qu Tenglong he advanced on Guazhou; Tenglong went deep and was attacked by rebels and killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he advanced on Guazhou with Qu Tenglong, who pushed too far, was ambushed, and killed in action.

sentences.zh: 德興阿率勁騎馳援，賊敗走，軍賴以全，賜號博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: De Xing'a led crack cavalry in hurried relief; the rebels were defeated and fled; the army was thereby preserved whole, and he was granted the title Boqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a led crack cavalry to the rescue, routed the rebels, and saved the army from destruction. He was granted the title Boqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 尋复敗賊三汊河，賊埋地雷誘官軍，德興阿偵知，揮軍繞路而前，賊伏壘不出，遂分軍兩路夾攻，斬馘過當，奪獲大砲地雷。

translations.literal: Soon he again defeated rebels at Sanhe River; the rebels buried land mines to lure government troops; De Xing'a detected this, directed the army to advance by a detour; the rebels lay in their stockade without coming out; he then divided the army on two routes for a pincer attack, beheaded more than was proper, and seized great cannon and land mines.
translations.idiomatic: He soon won another victory at Sancha River. The rebels had laid land mines to trap government troops, but De Xing'a discovered the ruse, swung his force around by a flank march, and when the enemy refused to leave their stockade, attacked from two sides. The slaughter was immense, and he captured heavy guns and the rebel mine stores.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，晉御前侍衛。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was promoted to bodyguard before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived he was promoted to bodyguard before the throne.

sentences.zh: 五年，迭攻瓜洲賊壘，又截擊竄賊於虹橋、八江口等處，皆獲勝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he repeatedly attacked Guazhou rebel stockades and also intercepted fleeing rebels at Hongqiao, Bakou, and elsewhere, winning every time.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he stormed the Guazhou rebel camps again and again and intercepted fleeing rebels at Hongqiao, Bakou, and other points, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 六年，托明阿兵敗於土橋，揚州复陷，諸軍渙散，獨德興阿軍未動。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Tuo Ming'a's army was defeated at Tuqiao, Yangzhou again fell, the armies scattered, but only De Xing'a's army did not stir from disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Tuo Ming'a's army was routed at Tuqiao and Yangzhou fell again. The armies scattered in rout, but De Xing'a's force alone held its ground.

sentences.zh: 詔黜托明阿，以德興阿為欽差大臣，加都統銜。

translations.literal: An edict removed Tuo Ming'a and made De Xing'a Imperial Commissioner, adding the rank of Commandant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Tuo Ming'a and made De Xing'a Imperial Commissioner with the rank of Commandant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 敗賊薛家樓，進規郡城。

translations.literal: He defeated rebels at Xuejialou and advanced to invest the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels at Xuejialou and advanced to threaten the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 賊萬人迎敵，德興阿身先士卒，斬賊酋一，諸軍乘之，賊大潰，乘勝复揚州。

translations.literal: Ten thousand rebels came to meet them; De Xing'a led from the front, beheaded one rebel chieftain, the armies pressed the advantage, the rebels were utterly routed, and taking victory in hand they recovered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand rebels came out to meet them. De Xing'a led the charge, killed a rebel chieftain, and the whole army pressed the advantage until the enemy broke completely. Yangzhou was recovered in the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 同時江浦、浦口並為賊踞，令總兵武慶攻克之。

translations.literal: At the same time Jiangpu and Pukou were both held by rebels; he ordered Regional Commander Wu Qing to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangpu and Pukou had also fallen to the rebels, and he ordered Regional Commander Wu Qing to recover them.

sentences.zh: 德興阿戰功素為江北諸軍冠，惟不曉漢文，命少詹事翁同書為幫辦。

translations.literal: De Xing'a's battle achievements had long been foremost among Jiangbei armies, but he did not understand written Chinese; Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent Weng Tongshu was ordered to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a's battlefield record had long been the best in the Jiangbei armies, but he could not read Chinese. Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent Weng Tongshu was appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 添調新兵，軍聲稍振，進規瓜洲。

translations.literal: Fresh troops were added and transferred; the army's reputation revived somewhat, and he advanced to invest Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh troops were brought in, morale improved somewhat, and he advanced against Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，參將富明阿破賊於土橋、四里鋪，水師又擊沉賊船，斬偽將軍陳磊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Regimental Commander Fu Ming'a defeated rebels at Tuqiao and Silipu; the naval force also sank rebel boats and beheaded the false general Chen Lei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Regimental Commander Fu Ming'a defeated the rebels at Tuqiao and Silipu, while the navy sank rebel vessels and killed the false general Chen Lei.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，合水陸諸軍進攻，毀賊艦及砲台。

translations.literal: That summer the combined land and water armies advanced in attack and destroyed rebel ships and batteries.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the combined land and naval forces attacked together and destroyed rebel ships and batteries.

sentences.zh: 德興阿親督戰，更番進逼，至十一月，大破之，复瓜洲。

translations.literal: De Xing'a personally supervised the fighting, pressing forward in relays; by the eleventh month he inflicted a great defeat and recovered Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a personally directed the fighting, pressing forward in relays until the eleventh month, when he won a decisive victory and recovered Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 賊負嵎歷四年，至是始克。

translations.literal: The rebels had relied on their lair for four years; only at this time were they taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had dug in for four years; only now were they finally overcome.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉調度有方，賜雙眼花翎，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised his skillful coordination, granted double-eyed peacock feathers, and gave him the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his skillful coordination, awarded him double-eyed peacock feathers, and granted him the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逼金山，剿平新河口、龍王廟等處餘匪。

translations.literal: Taking victory in hand he pressed on Jinshan and suppressed remnant bandits at Xinhekou, Longwang Temple, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage, he drove on Jinshan and mopped up remnant rebel bands at Xinhekou, Longwang Temple, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 江南軍亦同日克鎮江，專力進攻江寧。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan army on the same day took Zhenjiang and devoted its full strength to attacking Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan army captured Zhenjiang the same day and turned its full strength against Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 八年春，德興阿進軍江浦，獲勝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year De Xing'a advanced on Jiangpu and won.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year De Xing'a advanced on Jiangpu and won a victory.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊勢日蹙，悍黨陳玉成等由安徽糾眾來援，德興阿兵敗於浦口，退保六合，褫雙眼花翎，革職留任。

translations.literal: The Jiangning rebels' situation grew daily tighter; fierce faction Chen Yucheng and others gathered troops from Anhui to relieve them; De Xing'a's army was defeated at Pukou, fell back to defend Liuhe, was stripped of double-eyed peacock feathers, and dismissed from office but kept on duty.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jiangning rebels grew desperate, Chen Yucheng and other hard fighters rallied reinforcements from Anhui. De Xing'a was beaten at Pukou, fell back to Liuhe, was stripped of his peacock feathers, and dismissed from office though left on duty.

sentences.zh: 賊連陷江浦、天長、儀徵，德興阿不能救，揚州亦陷，褫世職。

translations.literal: The rebels in succession took Jiangpu, Tianchang, and Yizheng; De Xing'a could not save them; Yangzhou also fell, and his hereditary office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels overran Jiangpu, Tianchang, and Yizheng in succession. De Xing'a could not stop them, Yangzhou fell again, and his hereditary rank was revoked.

sentences.zh: 尋張國樑率兵渡江复揚州，而德興阿擁兵邵伯，觀望不前，嚴旨斥責。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Guoliang led troops across the river and recovered Yangzhou, while De Xing'a held troops at Shaobo, watched and did not advance, and was sternly rebuked by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang soon crossed the river and recovered Yangzhou, while De Xing'a sat at Shaobo with his troops, hesitating to advance, and was sharply rebuked by edict.

sentences.zh: 溫紹原守六合歷數年，為江北屏蔽，至是亦以援絕被陷，紹原死之。

translations.literal: Wen Shaoyuan had defended Liuhe for several years as the shield of Jiangbei; at this time he also fell because relief was cut off, and Shaoyuan died for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shaoyuan had held Liuhe for years as the shield of Jiangbei. Now, cut off from relief, the city fell and Wen Shaoyuan died defending it.

sentences.zh: 翌日而張國樑馳至，已無及。

translations.literal: The next day Zhang Guoliang hurried there, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang rushed up the next day, but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 國樑以江寧軍事急，移軍渡江，詔責德興阿規复六合，軍已不振，迄無功。

translations.literal: Guoliang, because Jiangning military affairs were urgent, moved his army across the river; an edict charged De Xing'a to plan recovery of Liuhe, but the army's spirit was already broken and in the end there was no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang shifted his army across the river because the Jiangning front was urgent. An edict ordered De Xing'a to recover Liuhe, but his force had lost its fighting spirit and he achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 何桂清疏劾：「德興阿秉性粗率，初賴翁同書相助，得克瓜洲。

translations.literal: He Guiqing memorialized in impeachment: 'De Xing'a's nature is coarse and rash; at first he relied on Weng Tongshu's help to take Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing memorialized: 'De Xing'a is coarse and rash by nature. He took Guazhou only because Weng Tongshu assisted him at first.

sentences.zh: 自同書調任安徽巡撫去後，左右無人，毫無謀略，貽誤軍事。

translations.literal: Since Tongshu was transferred to serve as Anhui governor, he has had no one at his side, possesses no strategy whatsoever, and has harmed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Weng Tongshu left for the Anhui governorship he has had no capable advisers, shown no strategic sense, and repeatedly bungled operations.

sentences.zh: 」和春亦劾其舉動乖謬，難以圖功。

translations.literal: ' He Chun also impeached him for perverse conduct, saying achievement was hard to expect.
translations.idiomatic: ' He Chun also impeached him for erratic conduct and said he was unlikely ever to achieve success.

sentences.zh: 文宗猶念其前勞，未遽加譴，九年，以圍攻六合久不下，革任召還。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong still remembered his earlier service and did not hasten to punish; in the ninth year, because the siege of Liuhe long failed to succeed, his post was revoked and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong still remembered his earlier service and did not punish him immediately. In the ninth year, because the siege of Liuhe dragged on without success, he was dismissed and recalled.

sentences.zh: 自此江北不置帥，軍務統歸和春節制。

translations.literal: From this time Jiangbei had no separate commander; military affairs were uniformly under He Chun's control.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Jiangbei had no separate commander-in-chief; all operations came under He Chun's control.

sentences.zh: 尋予六品頂戴，交僧格林沁差遣。

translations.literal: Soon he was given a sixth-rank hat button and placed at Sengge Rinchen's disposal.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given a sixth-rank hat button and assigned to Sengge Rinchen's command.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署密雲副都統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as acting Vice Commandant at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served as acting Vice Commandant at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 同治初，授西安右翼副都統，留辦山西防務，又移駐陝西同、朝一帶防剿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he was appointed Vice Commandant of the Right Wing at Xi'an, remained to handle Shanxi defenses, and was again transferred to garrison the Tong and Chao region of Shaanxi for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi he was made Vice Commandant of the Right Wing at Xi'an, stayed on to manage Shanxi defenses, and was later posted to the Tongzhou and Chaoyi sector of Shaanxi for defense and suppression.

sentences.zh: 五年，充塔爾巴哈台參贊大臣，授正紅旗漢軍副都統，幫辦新疆北路軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as Assistant Commissioner at Tarbagatai, was appointed Vice Commandant-in-Chief of the Han Plain Red Banner, and assisted in military affairs on the northern route of Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as Assistant Commissioner at Tarbagatai, was made Vice Commandant-in-Chief of the Han Plain Red Banner, and assisted in the northern Xinjiang campaign.

sentences.zh: 六年，丁母憂回旗。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother and returned to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, upon his mother's death, he returned to his banner for mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，依都統例賜卹，諡威恪。

translations.literal: Soon he died; according to the Commandant-in-Chief precedent funeral grants were given, and he was posthumously titled Weike.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward. Funeral grants were awarded according to the precedent for a Commandant-in-Chief, and he was given the posthumous title Weike.

sentences.zh: 論曰：勝保初以直諫稱。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Sheng Bao was at first known for blunt remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Sheng Bao first won renown for blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 及出治軍，膽略機警，數著功績。

translations.literal: When he went out to manage armies he was bold, resourceful, and alert, and repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the field he proved bold, resourceful, and quick-witted, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 然負氣凌人，雖僧格林沁不相下。

translations.literal: Yet he was overbearing by temperament and would not yield even to Sengge Rinchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was overbearing by nature and would not defer even to Sengge Rinchen.

sentences.zh: 自餘疆臣共事，無不齟《齒吾》互劾。

translations.literal: With the other frontier officials who worked with him there was none who did not clash teeth and impeach one another.
translations.idiomatic: With every other frontier official who served alongside him he clashed and exchanged impeachments.

sentences.zh: 文宗嚴馭之，屢躓屢起，蓋惜其才也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong disciplined him sternly; he stumbled and rose again many times—perhaps because his talent was prized.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong disciplined him sternly, yet raised him up again and again after each fall—no doubt because his talent was valued.

sentences.zh: 始終以客軍辦賊，無自練之兵，無治餉之權；

translations.literal: He always used guest armies to deal with bandits, had no troops he trained himself, and had no authority to manage supplies;
translations.idiomatic: He always fought rebels with borrowed armies, without troops of his own training and without authority over supplies;

sentences.zh: 撫用悍寇而紊紀律，濫收廢員而通賄賂，又縱淫侈不自檢束。

translations.literal: he pacified and employed fierce bandits and thereby disrupted discipline, indiscriminately took in dismissed officials and trafficked in bribes, and again indulged in debauchery without restraining himself.
translations.idiomatic: he enlisted fierce bandit leaders and thereby wrecked discipline, took in disgraced officials indiscriminately and trafficked in bribes, and indulged debauchery without restraint.

sentences.zh: 卒因袒庇苗沛霖，與楚軍不相能，朝廷苦心調和而不之喻，遂致獲罪，功過固莫掩也。

translations.literal: In the end, because he shielded Miao Peilin and could not get along with the Chu army, the court labored to reconcile them without his understanding, and he thus came to guilt; merits and faults surely cannot be covered over.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he fell because he shielded Miao Peilin and could not work with the Hunan army, though the court tried hard to reconcile them and he would not listen. His merits and faults cannot be hidden.

sentences.zh: 托明阿、德興阿皆戰將，非獨當一面之才，負乘僨事，宜哉。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a and De Xing'a were both battle generals, not talents fit to hold a front alone; to bear a burden beyond their capacity and ruin the affair—this was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a and De Xing'a were fighting generals, not men fit to command a theater on their own. That they were promoted beyond their capacity and brought disaster upon themselves was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 斯又不足與勝保並論矣。

translations.literal: These again are not sufficient to be discussed on the same level as Sheng Bao.
translations.idiomatic: They scarcely merit comparison with Sheng Bao at all.
